articles.title: Akademy 2026 in Graz
articles.desc: Two weekends ago, I spent around 24 hours in a train to go to and back from Graz to attend Akademy. This year was a bit special since we are celebrating the 30 years of KDE and this was also my first time attending as a member of the KDE e.V. board. Unfortunately I could only attend the weekend as I
articles.content: Two weekends ago, I spent around 24 hours in a train to go to and back from Graz to attend Akademy. This year was a bit special since we are celebrating the 30 years of KDE and this was also my first time attending as a member of the KDE e.V. board. Unfortunately I could only attend the weekend as I was also expected at the Nextcloud Community Conference in Berlin during the week. I attended a bunch of talks, one of my favorite was “Are we really going to use the same Desktop UX forever?” from Scott Jenson , which I found super interesting and insightful. It really was a call for us to try to innovate and experiment with new UX concepts and he proposed some interesting directions, where we could be going. A good wake up call that now that macOS and Windows are not inventing anything anymore on the desktop we should be driving UX changes forward. I also very much liked the talk “What Has Been Brewing in KDE PIM Land?” from Dominique Michel and arnaud chirat . As a fellow PIMster, it is great to see some real progress on fixing some longstanding issue in the backend. It’s great to see the Sovereign Tech Agency investing in this core technology. This also motivated me to spend some time on improving Merkuro again (more on that in a separate post). Aside from that, as always it’s great to meet up with my fellow KDE developers, share some drinks, exchange ideas or just catch up. On Saturday evening, I attended the sponsors dinner to discuss a bit with our sponsors. Akademy is a free event to attend and we are very grateful about companies sponsoring us to make it happen. Sunday morning, I went for a short stroll across the city, because while I was only staying for the weekend, I still wanted to discover Graz at least a bit. articles.title: 6 Popular Used Chevrolet Hybrids Ranked By MPG
articles.desc: Chevrolet only ever offered six models as hybrids in America, and buyers who want a Chevy that saves money at the pump can now buy them all used.
articles.content: 6 Popular Used Chevrolet Hybrids Ranked By MPG 6 Popular Used Chevrolet Hybrids Ranked By MPG If we only focused on new Chevy hybrids, this would be a very short article. The Bowtie brand currently sells only one hybrid vehicle in the United States: the Corvette. However, it is available in two different variants — both blending V8 muscle with electrified hybrid torque. The more fuel-efficient of the two trims is the 2027 that the EPA lists at 15 mpg city/24 mpg highway/18 mpg combined, while the brand's hybrid range-topper is the rated at 12 mpg city/19 mpg highway/14 mpg combined. Of course, since these hybrid 'Vettes feature 721 and 1,250 horsepower, respectively, their owners are unlikely to care. Chevy hasn't been all that invested in hybrids in the past, either. In fact, with the brand only ever selling six nameplates with hybrid power in the U.S., we've got room to touch on them all today — presented from least to most fuel-efficient. We based our rankings on the highest individual EPA grade, whether it's city, highway, or combined, for the Chevrolet Silverado, Chevrolet Tahoe, Chevrolet Corvette, Chevrolet Impala, Chevrolet Malibu, and Chevrolet Bolt. In cases where vehicles have had two different hybrid systems, we picked the one with the highest fuel-economy ratings. 2009-2013 Chevrolet Silverado: 22 mpg highway It's history time! General Motors first got into the hybrid game with the 2004 Chevrolet Silverado, but the truck was what we'd . This means very little of the Silverado's 42-volt battery system went to actually driving the vehicle. The setup was primarily for running accessories with the engine off during certain situations — and for powering the truck's four 110-volt outlets for tools and whatnot. In the end, the rear-wheel-drive models with the 5.3-liter V8 scored 17 mpg combined with the hybrid system and 16 mpg without, while the results for the 4X4 model compared at a 16 mpg versus 15 mpg combined. Notably, the hybrid system improved the 4WD Silverado's EPA scores by 15% in the city. Chevy dropped the Silverado hybrid after the 2007 model year, eventually reviving the truck for 2009 through 2013 with a new, two-mode hybrid system originally developed in concert with BMW and Chrysler. Without getting too deep into the details, the setup integrated two electric motors with the transmission to allow two separate assistance profiles depending on how fast the truck was going. The system could be relatively effective, too. Now relying on a 6.0-liter mill, the two-mode Silverado came in at 21 mpg in the city, 22 on the highway, and 21 combined in RWD and 20 mpg in all categories in 4WD. That's a 40% improvement over the city numbers in the most efficient gas-only truck — which carries the 5.3-liter V8. 2008-2013 Chevrolet Tahoe: 22 mpg highway Unsurprisingly, many of the numbers for the Silverado two-mode hybrid transfer over to its Chevrolet Tahoe platform-mate. The 2008-2013 Tahoe hybrid has the same two-mode technology, the same engine, and the same EPA ratings as the 2009 Silverado. And yes, as you can tell by those dates, the Tahoe was actually first to the market. Chevrolet's full-size body-on-frame SUVs did diverge from the brand's hybrid strategy in other ways. For instance, Chevy never tried out its mild-hybrid setup on the Tahoe or its extended-length variant, the Suburban. The Suburban wasn't configured with the two-mode setup either. GM did, however, follow its usual template with its Professional Grade division. The GMC Sierra had mild and two-mode hybrid systems in parallel with the Silverado, and the Yukon matched the Tahoe with a two-mode hybrid. The Yukon XL, like the Suburban, missed out on any hybrid help during this time. 2024-2026 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray: 25 mpg highway While those 2026 ZR1X models we mentioned at the start are fresh additions to Chevy's lineup, it's already possible to find them on the used-car market. articles.content: U.S. employers added a disappointing 29,000 jobs and the unemployment rate ticked up last month, the government reported Friday. Hiring dropped from a revised 133,000 in August, the Labor Department said. The unemployment rate rose to a still-low 4.2% from 4.1% in August. Meanwhile, the average long-term U.S. mortgage rate jumped this week to its highest level in nearly three years. The benchmark 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose to 7.28% from 7.03% last week, mortgage buyer Freddie Mac said Thursday, the biggest leap in several years. A year ago, the average rate was 6.34%.

articles.title: Newly discovered hair cells on squid may offer clues to understanding hearing loss in humans
articles.desc: Scientists have known for years that squid have cells with bundles of tiny, hairlike protrusions on their heads and arms, similar to those buried deep inside the human ear that allow us to hear. Now, researchers at Case Western Reserve University have discovered that these animals have hundreds more
articles.content: Scientists have known for years that squid have cells with bundles of tiny, hairlike protrusions on their heads and arms, similar to those buried deep inside the human ear that allow us to hear. Now, researchers at Case Western Reserve University have discovered that these animals have hundreds more of these cells, called hair cells, lining the entire surface of their bodies. The discovery may provide researchers with an unprecedented window into how humans use—and lose—their hearing.

articles.title: CM to inaugurate Bio Connect 4.0 life sciences expo on Oct 8
articles.desc: CM to inaugurate Bio Connect 4.0 life sciences expo on Oct 8
articles.content: CM to inaugurate Bio Connect 4.0 life sciences expo on Oct 8 | Thiruvananthapuram News - The Times of India CM to inaugurate Bio Connect 4.0 life sciences expo on Oct 8 CM to inaugurate Bio Connect 4.0 life sciences expo on Oct 8 Chief minister V D Satheesan will inaugurate the fourth edition of International Life Sciences Conclave and Expo on Thursday. Organised by Bio 360 Life Sciences Park under Kerala Lifesciences Industries Parks Ltd (KLIP), Bio Connect 4.0 expo will include more than 500 participants and 45 exhibitors, including international delegates. As a prelude to the conclave, a pre-event investors’ meet will be held on Oct 7 at Bio 360 Life Sciences Park. Industries minister P K Kunhalikutty said Bio Connect 4.0 will serve as a platform for stakeholder engagement, policy dialogue and collaboration, reinforcing Kerala’s commitment to emerging as a preferred destination for life sciences innovation, manufacturing and investment. “It will also showcase the infrastructure, facilities, support mechanisms and investment opportunities available at Bio 360 Life Sciences Park. Besides, the incentives offered under Kerala industrial policy will be highlighted,” he added. Kunhalikutty said the event would position Keralam as an emerging hub for biotechnology, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ayurveda, bioinformatics, nutraceuticals and other life sciences industries through a vibrant and collaborative ecosystem. Bio Connect 4.0 will feature a string of events, including keynote addresses, panel discussions, exhibitions, product launches by industry and startups, B2B and B2G networking sessions, showcases of R&D institutions and structured interactions that would facilitate technology transfer and industry partnerships. The major objectives are to attract industrial partners and investors from across the life sciences ecosystem to establish and expand their operations in Keralam, particularly at Bio 360 Life Sciences Park. It will focus on strengthening industry linkages and creating business, networking and partnership opportunities among stakeholders across the life sciences value chain. The event will also focus on fostering industry–academia collaboration by bringing together researchers, academic institutions, industry leaders, startups and policymakers to facilitate knowledge exchange and technological advancement. The conclave will also showcase Keralam’s model of responsible investment and responsible industry, innovation-led growth, sustainability, resilience and inclusive development. Spread across 200 acres of land at Thonnakkal in the capital city, Bio 360 Life Sciences Park has leasable, ready-to-occupy land parcels and is an ideal destination for global and domestic life sciences investments. articles.title: Digger and the Theater of Power
articles.desc: A skeptical review of Digger, starring Tom Cruise—a film that resists easy political labels and ultimately turns its scrutiny on the audience.
articles.content: A review of the 2026 satirical black comedy film directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu starring Tom Cruise and John Goodman, released by Warner Bros. he people running the world in Alejandro González Iñárritu’s have mastered everything except the job. They can command a room and invoke a higher purpose. Faced with an environmental catastrophe after an Arctic drilling accident has sent an enormous iceberg toward Europe, however, they struggle to work out what to do. The spectacle of their inadequacy makes for a wonderfully unnerving comedy: the world has assembled an extraordinary concentration of power and entrusted it to people who seem barely able to manage a meeting. But there is much more to the film than that. Its marketing presents a comedy about an environmental disaster caused by a vain, out-of-touch billionaire. Twice, however, takes a turn so ambitious and wild that revealing either would spoil the viewing experience. reminds me of the movies I would watch as a kid with my mom in the theater. If you go the bathroom or to get soda, you’ve missed critical scenes—when you get back to your seat you ask “what happened, what did I miss?” and it’s just not possible to explain. It is a brilliant movie, and you’ll be thinking about it for a long time. Go not knowing anything about it and avoid spoilers at all costs. This review was written so as not to give away too much of what makes the film so delightful to watch on the big screen. For much of the film, Tom Cruise plays Digger Rockwell, an aging oil magnate whose drilling operation has unleashed a vast mass of Arctic ice the size of Maryland that threatens to collide with Western Europe in three days, causing massive tidal waves across the North Sea. His attempts to confront the crisis bring him into contact with scientific advisers, the American political establishment (notably U.S. President Compson, starring John Goodman), and a European Parliament that has considerable trouble distinguishing a persuasive speaker from a responsible one. Across these encounters, Iñárritu keeps returning to a dispiriting mismatch between the qualities that win power and those required to exercise it. Cruise’s casting gives that mismatch a particular bite. His screen presence has so often promised that the impossible will get done. Here, the same confidence belongs to a man whose sense of his own importance has outrun his judgment. Digger can be appalling and still hold our attention; indeed, his ability to do so is central to the problem. John Goodman is superb as U.S. President Compson, who suggests a grotesque composite of Joe Biden, Mitch McConnell, and Donald Trump. The resemblance belongs to an entire exhausted political class as much as to any individual. Goodman makes the presidency feel immense and its occupant conspicuously unequal to it—old, out of touch, and physically incapable. The scientific advisers fare little better in practice. They struggle to explain the impending danger in terms their listeners (Digger, the president, military leaders) can grasp and turn their knowledge into a course of action. Being better informed than the president proves insufficient to change anything, to say the least. The public’s perception of the crisis seems to trouble the administration more than the crisis itself. What ought to be a search for solutions acquires the queasy logic of a public-relations meeting held during a fire—significant time is spent on managing the perception of the crisis on social media. A hilarious scene in which Digger and his environmental scientist eat tuna brings the same instinct to the dinner table. articles.title: US space factory platform signs first customer to screen drugs in microgravity
articles.desc: Exobiosphere will fly its automated drug discovery lab on Outpost’s reusable Space Factories platform returning samples to Earth for analysis.
articles.content: US space factory secures 1st microgravity drug research booking An automated laboratory designed to study diseases and screen drugs in microgravity has secured a place on a new US orbital manufacturing platform built to return research samples to Earth. Outpost Technologies on October 2 said that Exobiosphere has become the first announced commercial customer of its Space Factories platform. Under the agreement, Exobiosphere’s Orbital High-Throughput System, or OHTS, will fly aboard Outpost’s CarryAll spacecraft. The booking comes ahead of Outpost’s planned orbital mission in 2028. The companies aim to combine repeatable access to with sample return, allowing researchers to analyze their experiments after they reach Earth. Exobiosphere, a space biotechnology company headquartered in Luxembourg, is developing OHTS to support disease modeling, drug screening, and other orbital biology workflows. The automated laboratory is intended to help researchers investigate diseases and evaluate potential treatments in microgravity. Under the agreement, OHTS becomes the first customer research and manufacturing module slated to fly on Space Factories. CarryAll vehicles are intended to provide transportation and support the expansion of those activities. Returning biological samples is a central part of the approach. Researchers need access to those samples for further testing, validation, and development on Earth. Tiny 33-pound satellites track greenhouse gas emissions from 310 miles above Earth New center bids to supercharge nuclear isotope production for deep-space missions 3 missions in 13 hours: SpaceX launches astronaut crew, 130 satellites, and secret spy payload New prototype to test world’s first wireless power transfer between two spacecraft World’s most powerful rocket reaches orbit, deploys 26 Starlink V3 satellites Repeatable return could help Exobiosphere shorten experimental cycles and advance promising findings toward practical applications. “Microgravity accelerates biology in ways we simply can’t reproduce on Earth, and demand from researchers and pharmaceutical companies to run experiments in orbit already far exceeds the capacity of the International Space Station,” Space Factories combines reusable, free-flying CarryAll spacecraft with standardized containers and shared services. These include power, thermal management, data, and safety interfaces. The design allows customers to develop their own research or manufacturing modules while using a common spacecraft platform. Outpost says the expensive, complex infrastructure is built once and reused across missions, with the innermost module tailored to each customer. For Exobiosphere, that customized module is OHTS. The surrounding platform is intended to manage orbital operations, protect products, and support their return. “That’s exactly what we built Space Factories to serve: Exobiosphere brings the science, and we provide the standardized platform to fly it, operate it, and bring the results home. Their OHTS is a perfect first module,” said Jason Dunn, co-founder and CEO of Outpost. Outpost is developing the CarryAll vehicle family to host payloads in orbit and return cargo ranging from 200 kilograms to 10 metric tons. are designed to accommodate anything from a single experiment module to a larger commercial manufacturing payload. Their planned pressurized, ISS-compatible environment is intended to support sensitive research and technology payloads. Outpost also plans reusable returns, precision landings, and flexibility in landing destinations, giving customers a potential route from initial experiments to larger manufacturing operations. approaches its planned decommissioning in 2030. As commercial orbital platforms emerge, Outpost is positioning sample and product return as a core service for companies that need both access to space and analysis on Earth. articles.title: investingLive Americas FX news wrap 2 Oct: Nasdaq 100 closes at a record after soft US jobs; Treasury yields reverse higher
articles.desc: The US employment report gave stock buyers something to cheer about on Friday. Payroll growth missed expectations, earlier months were revised lower and wage growth slowed. The initial reaction was lower Treasury yields, a weaker dollar and higher stocks as traders reduced expectations for another O
articles.content: The US employment report gave stock buyers something to cheer about on Friday. Payroll growth missed expectations, earlier months were revised lower and wage growth slowed. The initial reaction was lower Treasury yields, a weaker dollar and higher stocks as traders reduced expectations for another October Fed hike. However, the bond market did not hold that move. Yields reversed higher and ended above Thursday’s levels. Stocks were more successful in holding gains, with the Nasdaq 100 closing at a new record. Nvidia and the Nasdaq Composite reached new all-time intraday highs, but neither finished at a record closing level. Dollar finishes mostly lower The USD ended lower against most major currencies despite the recovery in Treasury yields. The Australian dollar led the gains against the greenback, followed by the British pound and Swiss franc. The Canadian dollar was the exception. USDCAD finished higher as lower oil prices provided a less supportive backdrop for the CAD. The late-session levels showed: EURUSD: 1.1257, USD -0.14%. USDJPY: 157.82, USD −0.16%. GBPUSD: 1.3244, USD -0.34%. USDCHF: 0.8283, USD −0.29%. USDCAD: 1.4251, USD +0.23%. AUDUSD: 0.6958, USD -0.42%. NZDUSD: 0.5615, USD -0.21%. USDJPY illustrated the changing tone. The pair fell to 156.97 during the session but recovered toward 157.82 as yields moved back higher. Dollar sellers had their shot after the data, but could not hold the full decline. Treasury yields reverse the post-jobs decline The softer employment report initially supported Treasury buying. However, that buying faded, leaving yields higher across the curve 2-year yield: 4.8414%, +5.44 basis points. 5-year yield: 5.0733%, +6.83 basis points. 10-year yield: 5.2939%, +5.99 basis points. 30-year yield: 5.6448%, +4.18 basis points. The 10-year yield was back near 5.30% after trading toward 5.17% immediately following the report. That is an important distinction for traders. The employment data reduced the immediate pressure for further tightening, but the price action showed that it was not enough to sustain a bond rally. Inflation and the broader interest-rate outlook remain concerns. US stocks close higher; Nasdaq 100 sets a record All the major US indices finished higher, with the Nasdaq Composite leading the percentage gains. Dow industrial average: 51,182.11, +250.00 points or +0.49%. S&P 500: 7,722.85, +56.39 points or +0.74%. Nasdaq Composite: 27,190.86, +319.27 points or +1.19%. Russell 2000: 2,832.90, +26.27 points or +0.94%. Nasdaq 100: 30,807.93, +306.37 points or +1.00%, a new record close. The Nasdaq Composite reached a new intraday high but finished below its previous record closing level near 27,244. The Nasdaq 100 held enough of its advance to secure a new all-time closing high. Technology leads, but some record attempts fall short Technology was a clear source of strength, with both Nasdaq indices outperforming the Dow and S&P 500. Nvidia also traded to a new all-time intraday high, although it pulled back and finished below its previous record close. The softer jobs and wage numbers helped ease concerns about additional Fed restraint. Nevertheless, the recovery in yields created a less favorable backdrop later in the session. Small caps participated as well, with the Russell 2000 gaining 0.94%. The buying extended beyond the largest technology names, even as some of the record attempts fell short at the close. European stocks rebound Friday, finish lower for the week European equities closed higher on Friday, but the gains did not erase the weekly losses. German DAX: 25,222.05, +282.69 points or +1.13%. For the week, −0.73%. France CAC: 7,897.20, +61.88 points or +0.79%. For the week, −2.24%. UK FTSE 100: 10,461.94, +33.68 points or +0.32%. For the week, −2.18%. Spain Ibex: 19,085.31, +80.01 points or +0.42%. For the week, −3.12%. Italy FTSE MIB: 50,483.22, +245.36 points or +0.49%. For the week, −2.67%. European benchmark 10-year yields declined across the board on Friday. The weekly picture was more mixed: Germany’s yield fell 14.6 basis points, the UK’s fell 6.8 basis points and Spain’s declined 1.2 basis points. French and Italian yields rose 2.7 and 2.2 basis points, respectively, widening their spreads versus Germany. Employment growth slows; wages also disappoint The September jobs report was soft across several key measures: Nonfarm payrolls: +29,000 versus +90,000 expected. August payrolls: Revised to +133,000 from +162,000. Combined revisions to July and August: −60,000. Unemployment rate: 4.2% versus 4.1% expected and previously. Average hourly earnings: +0.1% for the month versus +0.3% expected. Annual wage growth: 3.0% versus 3.2% expected. Private payrolls: +46,000. Government payrolls: −17,000. Hiring was concentrated. Private education and health services added 20,000 jobs, construction added 11,000 and manufacturing added 9,000. Information, financial activities, and professional and business services all lost jobs. Over July–September, payroll growth averaged approximately 51,000 per month. Education and health services, construction and manufacturing together added more jobs than the overall payroll increase, with weakness elsewhere pulling down the total. There were some offsets. Household employment rose 406,000, while the labor force expanded by 485,000. Participation increased to 61.8%, helping explain the rise in unemployment. Average weekly hours held at 34.4, offering little evidence of aggressive cuts to working hours. The immediate market reaction pushed October hike probabilities toward 15%–16%. However, those were post-release readings, and the later rebound in yields showed that the broader rate debate remained open. Goolsbee keeps the focus on inflation Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee described the labor market as steady and said inflation was the more pressing part of the Fed’s mandate. He left both a hike and a pause available, while looking for evidence that inflation is moving toward 2%. For traders, the message is that one softer employment report does not settle the policy outlook. Slower wages are encouraging, but policymakers still want progress on inflation. Oil recovers after stockpile headlines push prices lower Oil fell sharply earlier after announcements of European crude and diesel stockpile releases. French President Emmanuel Macron outlined releases over four months, with G7 leaders confirming up to 100 million barrels. President Trump also said European diesel releases would begin immediately. However, sellers could not sustain the move below the $88.72 floor. The price recovered much of its earlier decline, with the late-session WTI futures snapshot showing $91.41, down $1.46 or 1.57%. Additional supply can ease near-term price pressure, but the rebound showed that sellers could not maintain control at the lows. Middle East developments and the broader supply outlook remain important for both energy prices and inflation expectations. Gold and silver decline despite the weaker dollar Precious metals failed to benefit sufficiently from the broadly weaker dollar: Spot gold: $4,142.55, −$34.84 or −0.83%. Silver: $60.509, −$0.4395 or −0.72%. The recovery in Treasury yields was a headwind for gold. Higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding a metal that pays no interest, helping explain why gold struggled despite the dollar’s decline. Silver also moved lower, while copper gained 0.69%, highlighting the different influences across the metals. Bitcoin does not follow stocks higher Bitcoin traded near $84,166, down $687 or 0.81% near the end of day. The gains in equities and weaker dollar did not translate into sustained buying in Bitcoin (click here for a technical look). The late rise in yields provided a less supportive backdrop, but Friday’s main observation was straightforward: stock-market strength did not carry through to crypto. Next week: Be aware. Be prepared. Next week’s calendar features US ISM services on Monday, Fed minutes on Wednesday, ECB meeting accounts on Thursday, and Canadian employment and University of Michigan sentiment on Friday. Inflation expectations in the Michigan survey will deserve attention. Stock buyers head into the weekend with gains and a Nasdaq 100 record close. However, elevated Treasury yields, the retreat from Nvidia’s and the Nasdaq Composite’s intraday records, and oil’s recovery from its lows leave some unfinished business. The first move after the news gives traders information. Whether that move can hold tells us more. Friday’s bond market was a good reminder of that. It’s a wrap. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.
